item.title: Spain’s Warren Buffett Followers Score a Rare Win for Value Investing
item.description: Madrid has turned into a value hub thanks to years of market-beating returns by Francisco García Paramés and his peers.

item.title: SoftBank Sells Yen Bond to Institutions at Year’s Highest Coupon
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. on Wednesday priced a ¥90 billion ($550 million) bond offering sold to institutional investors as the company broadens its funding sources at home and abroad to pay for its massive investments in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Debt Watchers Warn of Risks From Marcos’ Tax Relief Plan
item.description: The Philippines risks delaying planned reductions to its budget deficit if President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s tax relief proposals don’t come with revenue-generating measures, debt watchers said.

item.title: Unilever India Gets Rating Upgrades After Worst Day in Six Years
item.description: At least five brokerages upgraded Hindustan Unilever Ltd.’s shares following the consumer giant’s earnings, which triggered the worst selloff in more than six years on Tuesday.

item.title: Japan’s GPIF Boosts JGB Expertise by Employing Active Bond Funds
item.description: Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund hired active domestic bond funds for the first time in five years, a recognition that one of the world’s biggest retirement money managers needs to increase its expertise to deal with volatility in the nation’s debt market.

item.title: Wheat Futures Climb for Second Day as Black Sea Exports Falter
item.description: Wheat futures rose for a second session as escalating attacks between Russia and Ukraine threaten export prospects from two of the world’s top suppliers.

item.title: Sixth Street, SK Telecom, GIC Are Said to Vie for Bain’s Bridge
item.description: Investment firm Sixth Street Partners and South Korea’s SK Telecom Co. are among bidders for a significant stake in Southeast Asia’s Bridge Data Centres, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Korean Stocks See Record Wave of Trading Halts on Chip Selloff
item.description: South Korea’s stock selloff deepened as SK Hynix Inc.’s earnings disappointed, worsening the already‑jittery sentiment around artificial intelligence

item.title: HK Finance Stocks Eye Best Month in Two Years as Tech Hopes Wane
item.description: Financial stocks listed in Hong Kong are poised for their biggest monthly advance in nearly two years, with investors piling into banks and insurers as enthusiasm for technology shares fades.

item.title: Gold Flows to Hong Kong Hit Decade-High Before Clearing Launch
item.description: Hong Kong’s imports of gold surged to the most since late-2014 in June, driven by preparations for the city’s recently-launched clearing system as well as solid demand from mainland China.

item.title: Japan’s Tax Panel Chair Reiterates Proposal for 1% Food Levy
item.description: Japan should cut the sales tax on food and drinks to 1% and use cash handouts to offset the remaining 1 percentage point, the chair of a cross-party panel on the issue reiterated after the group failed to reach a consensus.

item.title: Indian IT Stocks Stage a Comeback as Global AI Trade Falters
item.description: The Nifty IT Index’s correlation with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has fallen to its lowest level since 2018.

item.title: South Korea’s Super-Aged Society Buoyed by Foreign Worker Uptick
item.description: South Korea’s population grew for a third straight year as an uptick in the number of foreign residents offset a continued decline in Korean nationals, underscoring the country’s growing reliance on overseas workers to ease the impact of rapid aging and a shrinking workforce.

item.title: Australia’s Unexpectedly Soft Inflation Puts Rate Hike in Doubt
item.description: Australia’s core inflation came in cooler than anticipated last quarter, giving the Reserve Bank scope to assess the outlook for the economy and prompting traders to slash bets on another interest-rate hike this year.

item.title: Japan Signals Steady Minimum Wage Gains, Backing BOJ’s Hike Path
item.description: Japan aims to keep minimum wages rising steadily, signaling income growth across a broad spectrum of the economy remains resilient as the Bank of Japan seeks evidence that pay gains are supporting domestic demand.

item.title: One SK Hynix Stock Trade Blew Up $60 Million in Crypto Bets
item.description: The crypto industry learned an expensive lesson this week when a Korean chip manufacturer’s shares suddenly dropped.

item.title: Korea-Hong Kong Correlation Shows Shorts Unwind: Equity Insight
item.description: Global funds entered short positions in Hong Kong tech stocks earlier this year to raise funds to invest in South Korea’s chip giants, but the latest correlation numbers show those trades look to be rapidly unwinding.

item.title: Capcom Shares Surge After Record Catalog Sales, 1Q Profit Beat
item.description: Capcom Co.’s shares gained the most since January 2014 after the Japanese videogame developer’s first-quarter operating profit beat analysts’ expectations, helped by strong software sales.

item.title: Malaysia Drops Blockchain Event Backing Over Ex-OnlyFans Star
item.description: Malaysia’s government withdrew its backing for a blockchain conference after promotional material of an after-party featuring a former OnlyFans creator sparked an outcry in the Muslim-majority country.

item.title: Bank Indonesia Says It’s Boosting Efforts to Support Rupiah
item.description: Bank Indonesia said it’s strengthening efforts to stabilize the rupiah, renewing a pledge to support a near record-low currency two days after the central bank’s chief abruptly resigned.

item.title: Woodside Natural Gas Output Slumps on Cyclone, Maintenance
item.description: Woodside Energy Group Ltd., Australia’s biggest natural gas exporter, said output slumped by more than a quarter in the three months through June after a cyclone that impacted operations and planned maintenance at its Pluto export plant.

item.title: Japanese Construction Shares Gain After Deadly Kyushu Earthquake
item.description: Japanese construction-related shares rose on expectations of rebuilding demand following a magnitude 7.1 earthquake on the southwestern island of Kyushu.

item.title: US Says Ex-Goldman Banker Berko Paid a ‘Holy Rain’ of Bribes
item.description: A former Goldman Sachs Group Inc. banker went on trial Tuesday for allegedly paying government officials in Ghana a “holy rain” of bribes to secure a lucrative power plant deal for a client.

item.title: Gold Edges Lower as Traders Assess Prospects for Fed Rate Hike
item.description: Gold edged lower ahead of a finely balanced interest-rate decision by the Federal Reserve due later Wednesday.

item.title: Hong Kong Data Center Loan Sale Shows Banks Hitting Sector Limits
item.description: An attempt by a lender to offload a portion of a loan backing a Hong Kong data center project is highlighting a global trend of banks reshuffling lending to keep exposure to the booming sector within limits.

item.title: Burnham Faces £24 Billion Squeeze From UK Inflation, NIESR Says
item.description: Public services in the UK face a £24 billion ($31.9 billion) hit in the current parliamentary term as higher energy prices and inflation eat into departmental budgets, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research warned.

item.title: Hike or Hold? Fed’s Warsh Has Markets Unsure: Decision-Day Guide
item.description: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady when it concludes its two-day meeting Wednesday, but market participants are eyeing the possibility of a surprise hike as patience with high inflation wears thin.

item.title: SK Hynix’s Profit Jump Misses Markets’ Lofty AI Expectations
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s quarterly profit rose 557%, but missed expectations, fueling fears that an AI boom that has propelled the semiconductor industry may be decelerating.

item.title: Oil Jumps After Iran Attack, US Stock Futures Dip: Markets Wrap
item.description: Crude oil jumped and US equity-index futures fell after fighting erupted in the Middle East, reigniting tensions after several days of calm and reviving concerns over energy supplies.

item.title: OpenAI Models Compromised a Customer at a Second Tech Firm
item.description: An OpenAI artificial intelligence agent that breached systems at the startup Hugging Face Inc. earlier this month also compromised a customer of the technology company Modal.
